items.description: Create persistent, file-based task plans that survive session resets when tackling complex multi-step agent work.
items.summary: The planning-with-files skill implements Manus-style persistent markdown planning for complex agent tasks spanning many tool calls. It creates `task_plan.md` for phases and decisions, `findings.md` for research discoveries, and `progress.md` for session logs, treating the filesystem as durable working memory beyond the context window. Critical rules include creating a plan before work, the two-action rule to save multimodal findings immediately, reading the plan before major decisions, updating status after each phase, and logging every error with a three-strike protocol before escalating. Hooks inject active plan context on prompts, remind agents to update progress after writes, verify completion on stop, and preserve state before compaction. Version 2.43.0 adds scoped plans under `.planning/`, SHA-256 attestation against plan tampering, parallel task workflows, and `session-catchup.py` recovery after `/clear`. Scripts initialize sessions, resolve active plans, and check phase completion.
highlights: Core trio: task_plan.md for phases, findings.md for research, progress.md for session logging.
Two-action rule saves browser and multimodal findings to disk before context loss.
Hooks inject plan data, block tampered attested plans, and remind progress updates after edits.
Supports parallel plans under `.planning/<slug>/` with active plan switching scripts.
Three-strike error protocol with mandatory plan logging and user escalation after repeated failures.

items.name: higgsfield-brandkit
items.author: higgsfield-ai
items.description: Build and extend full visual brand systems—palettes, SVG logos, typography, mockups, packaging, and brandbooks via Higgsfield CLI plus local tooling.
items.summary: Higgsfield-brandkit creates and extends complete visual brand systems through the Higgsfield CLI and bundled local scripts. It supports palettes, SVG logo marks, typography, mockups, social graphics, packaging, signage, merchandise, posters, decks, and editable brandbooks while preserving supplied official assets. A Brand Lock records constraints, approvals persist in local state, and downstream outputs regenerate only when foundation slots change. Use for new identities or applying existing branding across deliverables—not for general unbranded image generation or website implementation.
highlights: Persistent approval state with dependent regeneration rules
Recraft vector logos, palette boards, and deterministic PPTX/PDF brandbooks
Applies official assets without redesign when extending existing brands

items.name: higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail
items.author: higgsfield-ai
items.description: Generate high-CTR YouTube thumbnails and vertical video covers with identity-locked faces, logos, and surgical Seedream edits via Higgsfield CLI.
items.summary: Higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail creates click-worthy YouTube thumbnails and vertical covers through the Higgsfield CLI. It enforces truthful concepts, preserves up to three referenced identities, supports logos and controlled variants, renders with Nano Banana Pro, and applies focused Seedream edits for expression or background tweaks. The workflow covers intake gates, concept frameworks, prompt contracts, post-render vision QA, and optional headline overlays. Chain it after a video workflow when the topic is known; it is not for generating the video itself or product catalog shots.
highlights: Truthful information-gap concepts with up to three identity-locked references
Nano Banana Pro main renders plus Seedream surgical expression edits
Optional deterministic HTML text overlays and 16:9/9:16/4:5 ratios

items.name: nx-workspace
items.author: nrwl
items.description: Let their coding agent safely explore an Nx monorepo, list projects, inspect configurations, and understand task dependencies before running commands.
items.summary: Explore and understand Nx workspaces with read-only exploration of workspace structure, project configuration, available targets, and dependencies. Provides commands for listing projects with filtering by pattern, tags, and targets; viewing full resolved project configuration; checking target executors and options; and analyzing workspace dependencies. Essential for debugging nx command failures and understanding workspace layout.
highlights: Project discovery with filtering by pattern, tag, type, and target
Full resolved configuration via nx show project --json including inferred targets
Workspace-level configuration in nx.json with targetDefaults and namedInputs

items.name: golang-code-style
items.author: samber
items.description: Teach agents the idiomatic Go style that clearly signals developer intent through deliberate zero-value versus explicit initialization.
items.summary: Go code style skill covering clarity and readability beyond what linters enforce. Teaches semantic line breaking, variable declaration patterns, control flow design, function organization, and naming conventions. Emphasizes 'Clear is better than clever' with idiomatic patterns for large codebases.
highlights: Line-breaking rules for semantic clarity beyond column limits
Variable declarations: := vs var distinction for intent signaling
Control flow reduction: early returns, switch over if-else chains

items.name: insforge
items.author: InsForge
items.description: Bootstrap InsForge-backed services, schemas, and core platform primitives when standing up a new backend or agent-facing product on the InsForge stack.
items.summary: insforge is an insforge/insforge-skills agent skill for bootstrapping new backends on the InsForge platform. It guides developers through standing up InsForge-backed services, defining schemas, and wiring core platform primitives when starting agent-facing or API-first products. Use insforge at project kickoff instead of hand-rolling auth, storage, and service scaffolding from scratch. The skill targets teams committed to InsForge conventions for backend layout, data models, and integration hooks agents can call. Reach for it when prompts mention InsForge setup, schema bootstrap, or greenfield backend creation on the InsForge stack.
highlights: InsForge project bootstrap
Core schema and services
Platform primitive setup
Backend conventions
Agent-ready APIs

items.name: pexo-agent
items.author: pexoai
items.description: Generate complete short videos from a single text prompt.
items.summary: pexo-agent is a full video production agent that turns natural language descriptions into finished, publish-ready videos. It automatically selects the best video model per shot, handles multi-shot sequencing, adds music and subtitles, and performs lip sync. A 30-second product ad typically renders in under 10 minutes.
highlights: AI video generation with auto model selection across 10+ models
Full post-production pipeline: multi-shot, music, subtitles, lip sync
Supports 5 input types: text, image, URL, script, audio

items.name: insforge-cli
items.author: InsForge
items.description: Run Insforge CLI commands correctly for auth, project setup, and service operations so agents automate platform tasks from the terminal.
items.summary: insforge-cli is an Apache-2.0 agent skill from insforge/insforge-skills at version 1.9.0 that teaches agents to manage InsForge cloud backends exclusively via npx @insforge/cli commands. Core rules require JSON output for automation, server-only API keys, migration-first schema changes with db migrations new and db migrations up --all, and memory remember for cross-session project facts. The skill maps command areas across login, projects, billing, organizations, backups, database SQL and RLS references, storage, edge functions, AI OpenRouter setup, Stripe and Razorpay payments, deployments, compute, secrets, schedules, backend branches, logs, diagnose, PostHog, and Apify web scraping. Six documented exit codes distinguish auth, linking, not-found, and permission failures. Developers reach for it when prompts mention InsForge provisioning, RLS policies, edge function deploys, or backend branch merges instead of hand-rolled HTTP calls that bypass the CLI. Pair with the insforge app-integration skill when writing @insforge/sdk application code.
highlights: Insforge CLI command guidance
Terminal-first platform workflows
Project setup and auth patterns
Agent-safe command sequencing
Bridges local dev to Insforge services

It covers user operations, organization management, session handling, webhook configuration, and API authentication. Developers use it to build backend integrations with Clerk authentication and manage user lifecycle operations programmatically.
highlights: REST API explorer and reference for Clerk backend operations
Covers user management, organizations, sessions, and webhooks
Supports Clerk CLI operations and environment configuration

items.name: golang-error-handling
items.author: samber
items.description: Ensure consistent, production-grade error handling and structured logging when writing Go backend services and HTTP APIs.
items.summary: Go error handling skill covering idiomatic error creation, wrapping with context, inspection patterns, and production logging. Teaches the single handling rule (log or return, not both), sentinel errors, custom error types, panic/recover design, and structured logging with slog.
highlights: Error wrapping with %w for chain inspection via errors.Is/As
Single handling rule: errors logged OR returned, never both
Structured logging with slog and samber/oops for production errors

items.name: golang-testing
items.author: samber
items.description: Generate production-grade table-driven tests, testify suites, mocks, fuzz tests, and snapshot tests for Go services and CLIs.
items.summary: Go testing skill covering production-ready test patterns including table-driven tests, parallel execution, fuzzing, integration testing with build tags, and goroutine leak detection with goleak. Teaches test structure, naming conventions, and CI best practices.
highlights: Table-driven tests with named subtests for every scenario
Parallel test execution with t.Parallel() and goroutine leak detection
Fuzzing, integration tests with build tags, and deterministic goroutine testing

items.name: gws-tasks
items.author: googleworkspace
items.description: Create, update, list, and manage Google Tasks and task lists directly from the terminal or within agent workflows.
items.summary: gws-tasks provides agent and CLI access to Google Tasks and task lists through the Google Workspace CLI. It supports full CRUD operations against the Google Tasks API v1, including task list management, task creation/update/deletion, and clearing completed tasks. Developers use it to build task management workflows and agent-driven automation.
highlights: Full CRUD support for tasklists and tasks
Handles assigned tasks in Docs and Chat Spaces
Up to 2000 task lists per user with 20,000+ tasks per list

items.description: Generate verified webhook handlers that react to Clerk user, session, organization, billing and payment events.
items.summary: clerk-webhooks is an official Clerk skill that outputs complete webhook route handlers with signature verification on every handler. It covers user, session, organization, billing, and payment events for event-driven features like database sync, notifications, and third-party integrations. A developer uses it to add Clerk-driven side effects instead of polling the Backend API. Handlers verify with verifyWebhook and require a CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET.
highlights: Verifies every handler with verifyWebhook(req)
Covers user, session, org, billing, and payment events
Framework-specific packages (Next.js, Express, etc.)
Requires CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
Includes DB-sync and notification examples

items.name: remotion
items.author: google-labs-code
items.description: Automatically turn Stitch screen designs into polished product walkthrough videos with smooth transitions, zooms, and text overlays.
items.summary: The remotion skill from Google Labs Stitch creates walkthrough videos by combining Stitch screen retrieval with Remotion programmatic video generation. Prerequisites include Stitch MCP, Remotion MCP or CLI, Node.js, and a Stitch project with designed screens. The workflow discovers MCP server prefixes, lists projects and screens, downloads screenshots and optional HTML code, stages assets under assets/screens, and builds a screens.json manifest with titles, dimensions, and durations. Remotion setup checks for remotion.config.ts or scaffolds a blank TypeScript video project with @remotion/transitions and @remotion/animated-emoji. Architecture uses ScreenSlide.tsx for per-screen zoom and fade, WalkthroughComposition.tsx for sequenced transitions, and config.ts for fps and dimensions. Execution covers Remotion Studio preview, timing adjustments, and npx remotion render output. Advanced sections add interactive hotspots, voiceover sync, and HTML text extraction for automatic callouts on buttons and headings.
highlights: Retrieves Stitch project screens via MCP list_projects, list_screens, and get_screen with screenshot downloads.
Builds screens.json manifest and stages PNG assets for ordered walkthrough flows.
Scaffolds Remotion TypeScript project with ScreenSlide and WalkthroughComposition components.
Uses @remotion/transitions fade, slide, and spring zoom effects plus timed text overlays.
Renders final MP4 via npx remotion render or Remotion MCP with quality and codec options.
